title: Sahayak Jila Lok Abhiyojan Adhikari (Assistant District Public Prosecution Officer)
qualification: Candidates must hold aBachelor's Degree in Law (LLB)from a university recognized by the UGC. || The post is classified asGazetted, Second Class, and selected candidates are appointed on a3-year probation period. || Candidates must hold the required educational qualification certificateby the last date of online application; degrees awarded after the closing date will not be considered valid.
salary: Candidates asking about the salary for this post can note that the Sahayak Jila Lok Abhiyojan Adhikari post carries Pay Matrix Level-9, with a pay scale of Rs. 38,100 to Rs. 1,20,400 , in addition to Dearness Allowance and other allowances as notified by the State Government from time to time. This pay scale applies uniformly to both the regular and carry-forward/backlog vacancies advertised under this post. || In-Hand Salary Calculator
age_limit: The standard age limit is minimum 21 years and maximum 30 years as on 1 January 2026 , based on the date of birth recorded in the Matriculation or equivalent certificate. However, considering the interest of educated unemployed youth, the State Government grants local residents of Chhattisgarh a 5-year relaxation on the special upper limit of 35 years, effectively allowing local candidates to apply up to 40 years of age (this relaxation period currently runs from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2028). || On top of this, additional relaxations in the upper age limit are available as follows: || SC/ST/OBC (non-creamy layer) of Chhattisgarh:5 years relaxation on the higher age limit. || Government/corporation employees of Chhattisgarh (regular, temporary, or work-charge):upper age limit capped at 38 years. || Widowed, divorced, or separated women of Chhattisgarh:5 years relaxation. || Contractual employees of Chhattisgarh:relaxation equal to years of contractual service, capped at age 38. || Persons with disabilities:5 years relaxation. || Shiksha Karmi / Panchayat Karmi:relaxation equal to years of service, capped at age 45. || Candidates should note that all relaxations combined cannot push the maximum age limit beyond 45 years , and reservation/age-relaxation benefits are available only to bonafide local/domicile residents of Chhattisgarh.
application_fee: Candidates asking how much the CGPSC ADPPO 2026 application fee costs can note that it varies by category and domicile status, with an additional portal charge applicable to everyone. Local residents of Chhattisgarh belonging to SC, ST, or OBC (non-creamy layer), as well as local disabled candidates, pay Rs. 300 , while all other candidates, including those from outside Chhattisgarh, pay Rs. 400 ; in both cases, a portal fee plus GST is charged additionally to all applicants . || Candidates should also note that local residents of Chhattisgarh who actually appear in the written exam or interview will get their examination fee refunded to the bank account entered during the application process, though the portal fee, GST, and any correction charges are never refunded.
selection_process: Candidates curious about how CGPSC shortlists the Assistant District Public Prosecution Officer can note that selection happens in two stages: a written exam followed by an interview , with the written exam carrying 300 marks and the interview carrying 30 marks , for a combined total of 330 marks . The written exam consists of a single objective-type paper of 150 questions to be completed in 3 hours, with negative marking for wrong answers. || The exam paper is bilingual ( Hindi and English ), and the Commission may conduct it as a Computer Based Test (CBT) depending on the number of applicants. Negative marking is applied using the formula MO = M × R − (1/3) × M × W , where MO is marks obtained, M is marks per correct answer, R is the number of correct answers, and W is the number of wrong answers. To qualify, candidates must score a minimum of 33% in each paper for Unreserved category candidates and 23% for reserved category candidates ; there is no minimum qualifying mark for the interview . Candidates called for interview will be approximately three times the number of vacancies , drawn only from those declared qualified in the written exam, and the written exam will be held at centres in Ambikapur, Bilaspur, Raipur, Durg, and Jagdalpur (subject to change based on the number of applicants).
